English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
comprador
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Portuguese comprador (“buyer”), from Late Latin comparator, from Latin comparō (“to buy”), from con- (“with”) + paro (“to furnish”).

In Far East, originally applied to native servants in European households, later to native managers in European businesses.[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (rhotic) IPA(key): /kɒm.pɹəˈdɔɹ/
  • (non-rhotic) IPA(key): /kɒm.pɹəˈdɔː/
  • Hyphenation: com‧pra‧dor

Noun

[edit]

comprador (plural compradors)

  1. An intermediary.
  2. A native of a colonised country who acts as the agent of the coloniser.
  3. (nautical) A ship's chandler in the Far East.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • comprador bourgeoisie
  • compradorship

Translations

[edit]
intermediary — see intermediary
native of a colonised country who acts as the agent of the coloniser
  • Chinese:
    Mandarin: 買辦 / 买办 (zh) (mǎibàn)
  • Finnish: kollaboraattori (fi)
  • Japanese: 買弁 (baiben)

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Chisholm, Hugh, ed. (1911). “Comprador”. Encyclopædia Britannica (11th ed.). Cambridge University Press.

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From comprar +‎ -dor, or from Late Latin compārātōrem, from Latin compārō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾaˈdoʁ/ [kõ.pɾaˈdoh]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾaˈdoʁ/ [kõ.pɾaˈdoh]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾaˈdoɾ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾaˈdoʁ/ [kõ.pɾaˈdoχ]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾaˈdoɻ/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾɐˈdoɾ/ [kõ.pɾɐˈðoɾ]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾɐˈdoɾ/ [kõ.pɾɐˈðoɾ]
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /kõ.pɾɐˈdo.ɾi/ [kõ.pɾɐˈðo.ɾi]

  • Rhymes: -oʁ, -oɾ
  • Hyphenation: com‧pra‧dor

Noun

[edit]

comprador m (plural compradores, feminine compradora, feminine plural compradoras)

  1. buyer (person who makes purchases)
  2. customer
    Synonyms: cliente, freguês
